sections.html:
Eagle is an Ada County city about ten miles northwest of downtown Boise. The 2020 census counted 30,346 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 34,658. People sell here for many reasons: downsizing, a move toward family, or settling an estate. An heir in another state may want a closing that skips repeated trips, and cash involves fewer in-person steps than a typical listing.

The West Ada School District covers most of the city, with a small piece in the Boise School District, so verify the district for your address. Lot by lot, zoning, flood zone status and subdivision rules vary, and buyers will ask about all three.

A house in the mapped floodplain falls under flood rules, and a buyer's lender may require flood insurance. The city's floodplain brochure says a floodplain development permit must be obtained before any construction or development begins in the floodplain. That covers buildings, filling, grading, paving and excavation, and the rule comes from the Flood Hazard Overlay District in Title 10 of the Eagle City Code.

Standard homeowners insurance does not generally cover flood loss. Eagle takes part in the National Flood Insurance Program, which makes federally backed flood insurance available, and coverage is required in certain cases, such as buying with a federally backed mortgage.

Floodplain topicWhat the City of Eagle says
PermitFloodplain Development Permit before any construction, filling, grading, paving or excavation in the floodplain

City office660 E. Civic Lane, Eagle, ID 83616

Request the elevation certificate and permit history from the city before listing. Buyers who discover the floodplain only after an inspection sometimes walk, and giving them the documents first prevents that.

Dry summers and cold winters define the year, with about ten inches of snow and a winter low that averages 30.6 degrees Fahrenheit. Get the roof and the heating and cooling equipment inspected, study the grading around the foundation and note how the lot is irrigated. A house near the river deserves a second look at drainage and any sign of past water.

If you find a problem, a cash sale lets you sell without fixing it first. A buyer using a loan will usually ask you to repair it or lower the price.

Small jobs still help any sale. Clear gutters, check where downspouts discharge and photograph the yard in dry weather, so a later question about drainage has a straightforward answer.

Eagle houses follow the Ada County treasurer's calendar. Value is set from what a typical buyer would pay on January 1. Each taxing district may raise the property tax portion of its budget by no more than 3 percent, unless voters approve more or new construction and annexation apply.

  • Assessment notice: usually by the first Monday in June.
  • Appeal to the Board of Equalization: by the fourth Monday in June.
  • Full year or first half: December 20.
  • Second half: June 20.
  • Deed recording fee at the Ada County Recorder: $15.00.

The Recorder's Office is at 200 W Front Street, Room 1207, Boise, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Your closing agent will normally handle recording for you.

Most Eagle sellers must hand the buyer a completed property condition disclosure form. The requirement in section 55-2504 covers anyone planning to transfer residential property, including a rental that was never the owner's home. Some transfers are exempt under section 55-2505, such as fiduciary transfers, estate transfers, foreclosures, gifts to a spouse or lineal relative, and sales by an heir who has not lived there during the past year.

Section 55-2508 asks about the property's condition, and a house in or near the floodplain raises questions that fit that form. Answer honestly and attach the elevation certificate if you have one.

sections.h2: Renting short term before you sell
sections.html: Idaho has restricted local control here. Senate Bill 1162 of 2025 rewrote section 67-6539, so a city or county cannot pass or enforce a rule that bans short-term rentals, whether in so many words or in practice. If the house has been rented by the night, check with the City of Eagle and Ada County for any rules that still apply, and pull together the booking history buyers ask for.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale a good fit in Eagle?
sections.html:
Cash works when a firm closing date outranks the top possible price, or when repairs and showings are more than you want to take on. Eagle examples:

  • An estate sale where the heirs live out of state.
  • A house with floodplain paperwork or older systems that would slow a loan approval.
  • A rental that has lost its tenant.
  • A move for work or health reasons.

Cash Home Buyers makes as-is offers, charges you no commissions and no closing costs, and asks for nothing if you say no. Set our number beside a listing's expected net before you choose.

sections.h2: How a sale closes when the owner lives elsewhere
sections.html:
Estate sales are common in Eagle, and heirs are often scattered across several states. Start by asking the title company what each heir must sign and in what order. Then confirm who holds authority to sell, since estates and trusts have their own paperwork under the disclosure exemptions above.

On closing day the title company pays off any mortgage or tax balance from the proceeds and the Ada County Recorder files the deed. The recording fee is $15.00, and your closing agent normally handles that step. You do not need to visit the Recorder's Office on W Front Street yourself.

After closing, keep the settlement statement. If the house was in the floodplain, keep a copy of the elevation certificate and permit history with your estate records, because the buyer's insurer may contact you about them later.

sections.h2: Questions buyers ask about floodplain homes
sections.html:
Expect three questions. Is the house inside the mapped area? Is there an elevation certificate? Were permits pulled for any fill, grading or paving? Having those answers on one page makes a buyer's lender and insurer faster to respond.

Buyers using a federally backed mortgage will be told flood insurance is required in certain cases, and they will price a premium into their offer. A cash buyer reads the same documents but is not bound by a lender's rules, which is one reason floodplain paperwork rarely blocks a direct sale.

1. Order or locate the elevation certificate and permit history if any part of the lot is mapped as floodplain.
  2. Check which school district serves the address.
  3. Print the assessment notice and the treasurer's payment status.
  4. Tell the title company about heirs, co-owners or tenants so they can plan signatures and timing.
  5. Decide whether a listing or a direct offer suits your calendar.

Owners who live out of state can do most of this by phone and email, and the title company can arrange signing from a distance.

faqs.q: How far is Eagle from Boise?
faqs.a: Eagle is about ten miles northwest of downtown Boise, in Ada County.

faqs.q: Do I need flood insurance on an Eagle house?
faqs.a: It depends on whether the house is in the mapped floodplain and on the buyer's lender. The city says flood insurance is required in certain cases, such as buying with a federally backed mortgage.

faqs.q: When are Ada County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 20 for the full year or the first half, and June 20 for the second half.
Most of Eagle is in the West Ada School District, with a small part in the Boise School District. Confirm the district for your address.

faqs.q: Do I need to complete a disclosure form to sell my Eagle house?
faqs.a: Usually yes, under Idaho Code 55-2504, unless an exemption in section 55-2505 applies, such as a transfer by a fiduciary in an estate.
